chunks: "Pick-and-place is the machine that populates a board with surface-mount components.

After solder paste has been printed on the pads, the machine uses a vacuum nozzle on a moving head to pick a part from a feeder, usually a tape reel, checks it with a camera to measure its offset and rotation on the nozzle, and then places it on the board at the right coordinates and angle, pressing it gently into the paste.
It repeats that for every part on the board.

It knows where to place things from a centroid file exported from the CAD tool, which lists each part's X, Y, rotation and side, and it aligns the board using fiducials, so it corrects for the board's actual position.
There are fast chip shooters for passives, doing tens of thousands of parts an hour, and more flexible machines for large and odd parts like connectors and BGAs at lower speed.
The paste is tacky and holds the parts in place until the oven melts it."
